title: Annotatio V §.IV §VII: heirs-only goods; spiritual eating proper to heirs; Luther on promise/faith
pass_a_gloss: Resp. Lest we come to word-fights with the Author, let us posit (1) that under the name of Testamentary goods there come all the New Covenant’s Goods in general, and so also those which are common to the wicked equally with the Faithful; although meantime it is certain (a) that those Testamentary goods of the New Testament are properly so called in Sacred Scripture which fall to Christ’s heirs, and that Christ’s heirs are constituted only the sons of GOD: Whence the Apostle: And if sons, then also heirs — namely GOD’s heirs and Christ’s co-heirs, Rom. 8:17, Gal. 4:7. (b) It is certain that the Spiritual Eating of Christ’s Body — i.e. intimate communion with Christ — remains proper to Christ’s heirs. (c) It is certain according to Luther himself that every promise of Christ — among which the promise concerning eating Christ’s Body also finds place — cannot be obtained apart from faith, since without Controversy promise and faith are correlative, and where faith has not been, the promise is nothing (Tom. 2 Jena fol. 452 b. at end), and that only those are heirs who believe the Testament (ibid. fol. 455 a. at end).
pass_b_english: Reply (1): grant ‘testamentary goods’ can name all New-Covenant goods, even those common to wicked and faithful — yet Scripture properly calls testamentary those that fall to Christ’s heirs, and heirs are only God’s sons (Rom. 8:17; Gal. 4:7).

Spiritual eating (intimate communion) remains proper to those heirs. Luther: every promise — including eating Christ’s body — is nothing without correlative faith; only testament-believers are heirs (Jena Tom. 2).
source_text: Resp. Ne ad logomachias cum Autore deveniendum sit, ponamus (1) Testamentariorum bonorum nomine, omnia in universum N. Fœderis Bona, eóque etiam ea, quæ improbis juxta ac Fidelibus sunt communia, venire; licèt interim certum sit, (a) Testamentaria bona N. Test. in Sacrâ Script. illa propriè dici, quæ hæredibus Christi cedunt, hæredes autem, Christi solos DEI filios constitui: Unde Apostolus: Quodsi Filii, etiam hæredes, nempe DEI hæredes & cohæredes Christi Rom. 8, 17. Gal. 4, 7. (b) Certum sit, Spiritualem Manducationem Corporis Christi, i.e. intimam cum Christo communionem hæredibus Christi propriam manere. (c) Certum sit juxta ipsum Lutherum, tam promissionem Christi omnem, quas inter & promissio de Corpore Christi manducando locum reperit, citra fidem, obtineri non posse cum sine Controversia promissio & fides correlativa sint, & ubi fides non fuerit, promissio nihil sit, Tom. 2. Jen. fol. 452. b. in f. quam hæredes solos eos esse, qui credunt Testamento, ibid. f. 455. a. in f.
